title: Practical Round Count for Inner-Product Swap-or-Not
summary: The random-round-function analysis does not determine a practical round count for inner-product swap-or-not; the count needed for a good blockcipher remains open.

formal_statement.body: Determine a sufficient practical number of rounds $r$ for the inner-product realization of swap-or-not to behave as a good secure blockcipher: the theoretical analysis does not directly determine this value because its suggested random round functions differ substantially in computational cost from the inner-product round functions used in this realization; the unresolved task is to establish how large $r$ must be for this realization to provide a good blockcipher.

scope.domain: Cryptanalysis of the inner-product realization of the swap-or-not blockcipher construction.
parameters: r: number of rounds in the inner-product realization of swap-or-not
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine a sufficient practical value of r for the inner-product realization to provide a good secure blockcipher.

citations.label: An Enciphering Scheme Based on a Card Shuffle

progress.summary: The paper states that it does not know how many rounds make the Figure 5 construction a good blockcipher and leaves the round count for cryptanalysts to investigate. It cautions that its theoretical random-round-function analysis does not directly prescribe this value.
citation_labels: Viet Tung Hoang et al., An Enciphering Scheme Based on a Card Shuffle
